name: UserDefinedTypeRangeOption
docs:
Options for PostgreSQL `CREATE TYPE ... AS RANGE` statement.

Range types are data types representing a range of values of some element type
(called the range's subtype). These options configure the behavior of the range type.

# PostgreSQL Documentation
See: <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtype.html>

# Examples
```sql
CREATE TYPE int4range AS RANGE (
    SUBTYPE = int4,
    SUBTYPE_OPCLASS = int4_ops,
    CANONICAL = int4range_canonical,
    SUBTYPE_DIFF = int4range_subdiff
);
```
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: Canonical
docs: Function to convert range values to canonical form: `CANONICAL = canonical_function`
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: Collation
docs: Collation to use for ordering the subtype: `COLLATION = collation`
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: MultirangeTypeName
docs: Name of the corresponding multirange type: `MULTIRANGE_TYPE_NAME = multirange_type_name`
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: Subtype
docs: The element type that the range type will represent: `SUBTYPE = subtype`
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: SubtypeDiff
docs: Function to compute the difference between two subtype values: `SUBTYPE_DIFF = subtype_diff_function`
availability: Observed in the hosted documentation configuration; consumer features unverified.

name: SubtypeOpClass
docs: The operator class for the subtype: `SUBTYPE_OPCLASS = subtype_operator_class`
